text:
Education in Pakistan has a national system primarily inspired by the English educational system. Primary education, which runs from years 1 to 5, is attended by only about 67.5% of Pakistani children. The curriculum covers disciplines such as Arts, Computer Studies and ICT, General Science (including Physics, Chemistry, and Biology), Modern languages (Urdu and English), Mathematics, Religious Education (Islamic Studies), Social Studies, and Pakistan Studies.
Secondary education begins in year 9 and lasts for four years, requiring students to pass national examinations at the end of year 9 (SSC) and year 10 (HSSC). Alternative qualifications are available through bodies like the General Certificate of Education (GCE) or IGCSE, which are managed by British examination boards. Tertiary education involves professional institutes for various Bachelor's degrees (like medicine, law, and engineering) or general universities for Arts and Science degrees. A significant challenge across the system is the profound gender disparity, as illustrated by the fact that men have a literacy rate of around 67% versus women who have a literacy rate of 42%.
